newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem orders committee to probe Nazi activities.
newsitem.headline: Menem orders committee to probe Nazi activities.

text.p: President Carlos Menem on Thursday ordered the creation of a committee to investigate Nazi activities a day after a U.S. report criticised Argentina for having traded with Adolf Hitler's regime.

The body will include Argentine and foreign members and will probe "the entrance and presence of people, goods and assets" related to the Nazi era, the private news agency DyN said, quoting an official government decree.
According to U.S. documents recently declassified, the Nazis secretly sent more than $1 billion to be invested in Argentina one month before the Second World War ended in 1945.
Washington on Wednesday issued a report criticising Argentina, Spain and Portugal for having traded with Germany's Nazi regime.

The plan to form the committee was announced last month by Argentine Foreign Minister Guido di Tella, who said the group's investigation would be thorough even though it might touch on powerful former figures in the ruling Peronist Party.
Several historians have suggested that the first government (1946-1952) of the late Juan Peron, founder of Menem's party, had Fascist sympathies.

After the war Argentina turned into a haven for Nazis, among them Holocaust architect Adolf Eichman, doctor Jozef Mengele, and former SS officer Erich Priebke, currently in Italy after having been extradited for trial.
Menem's decree recalled that in 1992 his government opened secret archives related to Nazi activities and that it extradited Priebke to Italy.
Argentina is home to one of the world's largest Jewsih communities. In 1992 and 1994 two antisemitic bomb attacks in Buenos Aires killed more than 100 people.
